messages:
alex: FYI CVE-2026-2142 just landed in OSS advisory. Affects our libtls wrapper used by the hosted API and Dedicated runtime. Reported vector: remote renegotiation leading to potential session state leakage. CVSS 7.8 per vendor.
maria: :warning: can you paste the advisory link? we need to classify impact and SLA risks.
alex: https://security.example.org/CVE-2026-2142 (vendor) — short summary: exploit requires client-initiated renegotiation; affects TLS stacks < 1.2 compatibility and some custom renegotiation handlers.
raj: Quick triage: hosted API path uses the wrapper in the ingestion path; Dedicated has it in inference runtime container; Private customers may or may not be compiled with the vulnerable flag depending on distro. We need to know customer exposure surface by tier.
emily: Suggestion: mark as P1 for Hosted (public facing), P2 for Dedicated, P3 for Private/air-gapped until we confirm builds. Do we have telemetry on TLS renegotiation events? :eyes:
linda: Audit logs show <0.1% of sessions with renegotiation over last 90d across hosted. But large customers (enterprise accounts) have some legacy clients that do renegotiation. I can map top 10 customers by traffic to see overlap.
sec-bot: Automated note: dependency libtls v1.3.2 has patch 1.3.3 addressing CVE-2026-2142. Patch introduces a compatibility flag --disable-client-renegotiation and a forward-compatible API.
alex: Proposed rollouts:
- Hosted API: emergency patch + deploy to canary pool within 24h, full rolled out in 48h if no regressions.
- Dedicated: schedule canary on 2 reserved clusters (one us-west, one eu-west) within 48h, full deployment over 7 days with autoscaling maintenance windows.
- Private: publish advisory and patched package; offer assisted patch service. For air-gapped clients, provide signed binaries and KMS/key-rotation guidance.
raj: Important: patch touches TLS stacks and may require KMS key rewrap if we rotate keys. If we rotate keys mid-rollout, some older Dedicated nodes might fail to access encrypted config. Need a migration plan.
emily: Agreed. Plan: 1) deploy patched binary that understands both current key format and new rewrapped keys; 2) perform staged key rotation after canary success. That avoids downtime.
linda: Also RBAC/audit note: update audit pipeline so any key-rotation activity and deployment restarts are flagged for security review. Add a rule: deployment restarts during this window generate high-priority audit events.
alex: We need clear customer communication for Enterprise accounts: ETA for Hosted patch + potential short maintenance window for Dedicated enterprise clusters. Linda, can you coordinate account team notices? timeline: draft now, send in 2 hours.
linda: On it. I'll include mitigation steps they can take client-side: disable renegotiation, rotate TLS client certs, and validate pinned CAs.
sre-oncall: Maintenance windows constraints: we must avoid overlapping with nightly backup windows for Dedicated customers (00:00-02:00 UTC). Suggest canary in UTC 03:00 and broaden during low-traffic periods for each region.
alex: Decision checklist (agreed):
- Hosted: hotfix -> canary in 24h -> full 48h (P1)
- Dedicated: canary 48h -> staged 7d rollout, respect maintenance windows (P2)
- Private: advisory + signed patches + assisted option (P3)
- Key rotation: staged post-canary, binaries support old and new keys
- Audit: create alert for any deployment restarts and key rewrap ops
- Customer comms: enterprise notice within 2 hours, public advisory after Hosted canary success
raj: I'll own Dedicated canary and verification tests. test plan includes: TLS handshake fuzzing, live traffic replay, and latency SLO checks.
emily: I'll add regression checks to the CI pipeline and raise a rollback playbook. Put the rollback command in case we see errors:

```
# rollback to previous image
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/inference-runtime inference-runtime=redwood/inference:stable-2026-02
```

alex: Good. Also add a temporary routing fallback: route 5% of traffic to older pool if new image fails health checks.
linda: Draft message for accounts ready, will ping for review in 20m. tagging @account-eng for approvals.
sec-bot: Reminder: file incident ticket SEC-2026-2142 and attach this thread. https://tracker.redwood/SEC-2026-2142
alex: Thanks everyone. We'll sync on a short stand in 30m to finalize windows. :thumbsup:
